storyboard.ears: One stomach virus keeps finding its way onto ships packed with thousands of people.
Reported cruise outbreaks hit 20 last year, continuing a three-year climb.
storyboard.eyes: substance: yellow quarantine flags; cause: Data hauls the line hand over hand and the string of yellow quarantine flags rises up over the ship's mast, one more flag per outbreak
storyboard.evidence: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) | Cruise ship gastrointestinal illness outbreaks reported to CDC | https://www.cdc.gov/nceh/vsp/surv/gilist.htm | 2026-10-30

storyboard.ears: Norovirus alone caused 15 of those outbreaks, making one bug the main repeat offender.
storyboard.evidence: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) | Cause of 2024's cruise ship outbreaks | https://www.cdc.gov/nceh/vsp/surv/gilist.htm | 2026-10-30

storyboard.ears: Some cruise ships carry 7,600 guests at once, giving norovirus a huge crowd of close contacts to spread through.
storyboard.eyes: substance: guests lighting up cabins; cause: Data grips the luggage cart and pushes it up the gangway, and cabin after cabin lights up as the guests board
storyboard.evidence: Royal Caribbean International | People aboard the world's largest cruise ship at max capacity | https://www.royalcaribbean.com/cruise-ships/icon-of-the-seas | 2026-10-30

storyboard.ears: Crowded cruises give contagious illness thousands of chances to spread.
